title: Build a circuit breaker
summary: A dependency is down and every request still waits the full timeout for it to say so. Build the breaker that stops asking: three states, a counter, a wait, and one trial call to decide whether it is back.

checkpoints.title: Failures trip it
checkpoints.hint: The count is of consecutive failures, so a success sets it back to zero rather than subtracting one. Pass both the value and the error straight through: a breaker changes when a call is made, never what it answers.

checkpoints.title: An open circuit fails fast
checkpoints.hint: Throw CircuitOpenError before calling `fn`, not after. A refusal is not a failure of the dependency, so it must not move the counter or the deadline: derive the state from `openedAt` and the clock rather than storing it and mutating it on the way past.

checkpoints.title: A slow call is a failure
checkpoints.hint: Race `fn()` against `clock.sleep(timeoutMs)` and have the sleep resolve to a sentinel rather than reject, then throw CallTimeoutError when the sentinel wins. A rejection from the losing side of a settled race is an unhandled rejection later, when the clock passes it.

checkpoints.title: One trial call decides
checkpoints.hint: Half-open is not a fourth thing to store: it is what open means once `openMs` has passed. One trial at a time needs a flag of its own, cleared in a `finally` so a rejected trial does not wedge it, and a failed trial re-opens by moving `openedAt` to now.

checkpoints.title: The rules hold on schedules nobody wrote
checkpoints.hint: The report prints the schedule that broke a rule, shrunk to the fewest steps that still break it, and it is a complete reproduction: those options, those calls, in that order. `call(hang)` is a dependency that never answers, and the clock moves by `timeoutMs` while it is in flight. Read the last line first, because it names which rule went.
